name: Fruity fragrances

lead: Fruity fragrances are scents in which fruit notes other than citrus, such as peach, blackcurrant (cassis), mango, apple or pineapple, define the character. People wear them as part of grooming and style to smell fresh, youthful or approachable.

A widely cited reference point in men's fragrance writing is Creed Aventus, described by reviewers as a fruity-smoky 'pineapple smoke' scent. Retailer and review guides present lighter fruits such as apple and bergamot as daytime or office choices and heavier ones such as pineapple and blackcurrant as evening choices.

paras: Users apply fragrance to pulse points or clothing as the last step of grooming and choose by occasion: lighter fruity scents for day, richer ones for evenings. Many sample or decant before buying.

Fragrance can irritate or sensitise some skin, and scents are strongly subjective, so a note one person finds pleasant another may not. Fruit notes in perfumery are mostly built from synthetic or non-fruit materials rather than extracted from the fruit.

forums.title: Rebirth of the Juggernaut: Brute Force and Ignorance (Part 1)

chain: Choose a scent built on fruit accords
angle.text: Fruity scents are chosen to read as fresh, youthful and approachable. How a scent is perceived depends on the wearer and the people around them.

lead: Fruity fragrances are perfumes and colognes whose main accord is fruit. In the fragrance classification described in general references, the fruity family is defined as featuring fruits other than citrus, such as peach, cassis, mango and passionfruit [1].

Perfumery references note that fresh fruits such as apples, strawberries and cherries rarely yield the expected odours when extracted, so fruity notes in perfumes are more likely synthetic [1]. Most fruit aromatics in perfumery come from citrus rind [1].

For appearance and presentation, fragrance is part of grooming: it contributes to how a person is perceived alongside clothing and skin. In men's fragrance guides, Creed Aventus is repeatedly given as the reference fruity scent, with notes of pineapple, bergamot, blackcurrant and apple over a woody, mossy base.

paras: Perfume notes are arranged as top, middle and base. Fruit notes commonly sit in the opening and are paired with bergamot or other citrus, and with woods, musks or mosses in the base. The Fragrance Wheel, created by Michael Edwards in 1983, groups perfumes into families, and the fruity family is defined by non-citrus fruit [1].
François Coty's Chypre (1917) established the chypre structure of bergamot, oakmoss and labdanum, and fruity-chypre fragrances like Aventus combine fruit with that mossy base [1].

Online guides describe fruity men's fragrances as less common than woody or fresh categories, though sources vary on how common they are. Lighter fruits such as apple and bergamot are suggested for daytime and office wear, while pineapple and blackcurrant are suggested for evenings.
No studies found on fruity fragrances as a category and their effect on perceived attractiveness.
